item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-99d96e86c8b3085c","start_unit":5,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The Democratic Republic of the Congo signed the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons on 20 September 2017 and ratified it on 22 September 2022; the treaty status page lists it among the parties as of 1 August 2026.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Pre-2023 inherited context relevant to the ruler's 2023 nuclear-risk posture; no new 2023 action is shown.","ruler_attribution":"The treaty record establishes the DRC's state-level commitment; it does not identify Félix Tshisekedi's personal role in the 2022 ratification.","limitations":["The document provides no evidence of 2023 implementation, funding, inspection, or compliance activity."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3efa9a433eb24ee5","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The 2023 state budget was voted at USD 14 billion and later reported as executed at USD 13 billion in revenue (91.22% realization) and USD 13.86 billion in expenditure (96.49% execution). The account-rendering law was adopted by the National Assembly and Senate and promulgated by President Félix Tshisekedi on 20 December 2024.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The quantitative results concern the 2023 fiscal year; promulgation and parliamentary review occurred in 2024.","ruler_attribution":"Tshisekedi promulgated the 2023 accounts law; the reported execution figures concern the government and budget institutions collectively.","limitations":["The document does not establish that Tshisekedi personally selected or controlled each expenditure.","The figures are reported in a 2024 news account rather than accompanied here by the underlying audit report."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3efa9a433eb24ee5","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"During parliamentary review of the 2023 accounts, deputies and senators criticized incoherent spending, emergency procedures, weak provincial credit allocations, and noncompliance with the public-finance law.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5","5B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The findings concern execution of the 2023 budget and were raised during its later parliamentary review.","ruler_attribution":"The criticisms target the government and budget execution; the source does not attribute each irregularity directly to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The document summarizes parliamentary criticism without reproducing the full legislative or audit findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3efa9a433eb24ee5","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"Parliamentarians, citing observations of the Court of Accounts, identified excessive budget overruns in some portfolios, payment of uncertified debts, and budget text references to works for which no concrete field action was observed.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"These institutional findings concern the 2023 budget's execution and subsequent account review.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern public-finance management under Tshisekedi's government, but the source does not show his personal direction of the cited transactions.","limitations":["The article does not specify the portfolios, amounts, projects, or individual officials involved."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2e0cb79426999f79","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In July 2023, Tshisekedi directed the budget and finance ministers, the Central Bank governor, and the Inspectorate General of Finance to enforce measures aimed at stabilizing the exchange rate, with the prime minister responsible for follow-up and implementation. Measures included regular central-bank foreign-exchange intervention, limiting public spending to priorities through normal procedures, prohibiting cash payment of public expenses at the central bank, tighter oversight of exchange bureaux, tax withholding, and payment of taxes in Congolese francs.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7","5B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly dated to July 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The article reports Tshisekedi's directives and assigns implementation to named government, central-bank, and oversight institutions.","limitations":["The source reports the measures and an exchange rate of approximately 2,500 Congolese francs per US dollar but does not establish whether the measures achieved stabilization."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c6d0d5989bc18858","start_unit":1,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"An interministerial order signed on 15 September 2023 established how the state's share of REDD+ carbon-credit sale profits would be distributed: 50% to the Treasury, 15% to the province, 10% to the generating decentralized territorial entity, and 25% to the Environmental Intervention Fund, including 5% for FONAREDD. It required a six-month implementation evaluation and assigned execution to the environment ministry's secretary-general and the revenue administration's director-general.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","5B.10","6B.3","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly dated to September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The order was issued by the environment and finance ministers under the presidential-government framework; the text does not identify a personal Tshisekedi directive.","limitations":["The document establishes the allocation rules and planned evaluation, not actual disbursement or outcomes for communities or provinces."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b9c77b3efb01302a","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In a 3 November 2022 address, Tshisekedi said that, when facing the eastern security crisis, he chose diplomacy before war and described participation in regional processes seeking an immediate cessation of hostilities, disarmament, and a political process; he also described a Luanda roadmap calling for an end to hostilities and M23 withdrawal.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.10","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Pre-2023 policy context carried into the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The statements and described decisions are directly attributed to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source is a presidential address from 2022 and does not establish implementation or durable results during 2023.","The account presents the presidency's characterization of the conflict and diplomatic efforts."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b9c77b3efb01302a","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The same address stated that more than 200,000 people had been displaced by fighting in Rutshuru and that Tshisekedi had given the government precise instructions to gather and care for displaced people, including shelter, food, and health support.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.6","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The displacement and directive are from November 2022 and provide inherited crisis context for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The address directly attributes the instructions to Tshisekedi and their implementation responsibility to the government.","limitations":["The source does not provide evidence of the resources delivered, geographic coverage, or outcomes of the assistance."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-e6464762de0d7d30","SRC-7eb737899460d510","SRC-7679ca736b8d4cdd","SRC-9c65a8fc202e097d","SRC-98c1922ae4f61105","SRC-0611072cf7e1e1f6","SRC-5e40e54281ebc8a7"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied documents concern periods outside 2023 or provide only generic institutional information, so they do not yield material 2023 facts for Félix Tshisekedi's 1B-8B lenses."]}
